concept.name: String Matching Algorithms

relationships.description: Connects String Matching Algorithms to core algorithm patterns in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: String matching algorithms locate exact or multi-pattern substrings in linear or sublinear time without naive O(N*M) backtracking, using prefix tables (KMP), bad-character jumps (Boyer-Moore), rolling hashes (Rabin-Karp), or failure-link tries (Aho-Corasick).
spark.keyTakeaway: Match the algorithm to the cardinality and alphabet: KMP guarantees O(N + M) worst-case for single patterns, Boyer-Moore/Two-Way powers fast single-pattern scans like grep/std::search, Rabin-Karp handles 2D/plagiarism hashing, and Aho-Corasick matches 10,000+ keywords simultaneously in a single O(N + Z) pass.

concept.whyItMatters: Naive nested-loop matching degrades to O(N * M) on repetitive inputs (like DNA or crafted regex/HTTP payloads), creating CPU DoS vulnerabilities; linear-time automata keep WAFs, log scanners, and search engines predictable at gigabytes per second.
whenToUse: Single-pattern exact search with strict O(N + M) worst-case guarantees on adversarial or repetitive inputs (KMP / Z-algorithm).
High-throughput single-pattern search in large ASCII/UTF-8 logs or source files where skipping ahead by M characters cuts cache reads (Boyer-Moore / Boyer-Moore-Horspool).
Multi-pattern scanning against thousands of signatures—such as DLP, WAF rules, antivirus, or profanity filters—in one pass (Aho-Corasick).
whenNotToUse: Full-text natural language search with stemming, fuzzy typos, or BM25 ranking—use an inverted index (Lucene/OpenSearch) or edit-distance/FST.
Complex regular expressions with backreferences—use RE2/DFA-based engines rather than raw exact-match algorithms.
One-off short strings (< 1 KB) where Python's `in` (Two-Way / fastsearch) or Java's `String.indexOf` already runs optimized native C/intrinsic SIMD code.
keyPoints: Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) precomputes an LPS (Longest Proper Prefix which is also Suffix) array in O(M) time so the text pointer never moves backward, guaranteeing O(N + M) worst-case.
Boyer-Moore compares right-to-left and uses bad-character + good-suffix heuristics to skip up to M characters per mismatch, achieving sublinear O(N / M) average time on large alphabets.
Rabin-Karp computes a polynomial rolling hash in O(1) per slide, making it ideal for multi-pattern equal-length matching and 2D matrix/plagiarism fingerprinting.
Aho-Corasick builds a Trie augmented with KMP-style failure links and dictionary-suffix links, scanning text in O(N + Sum(M_i) + Z) regardless of how many thousands of patterns exist.
Standard libraries already optimize exact search: CPython uses a Boyer-Moore-Horspool/Sunday hybrid (`fastsearch`), while JVM intrinsics vectorize `String.indexOf` with SIMD.

examples.title: DLP & WAF multi-signature scanner with Aho-Corasick
examples.scenario: An API gateway inspects 50 MB/s of JSON payloads against 12,000 sensitive-keyword and SQLi signatures; running 12,000 separate regexes or `contains()` calls takes 180 ms per 1 MB payload.
examples.outcome: Compiling the 12,000 signatures into a single Aho-Corasick automaton cuts scan time to 1.4 ms per 1 MB payload in a single linear pass with zero backtracking.

examples.title: Streaming DNA / log motif search with KMP
examples.scenario: A Java log processor scans multi-gigabyte streaming chunks for repetitive binary/text markers without buffering the whole file in memory.
examples.outcome: KMP's state machine tracks only the current LPS index `j` across chunk boundaries, guaranteeing O(N) streaming throughput with O(M) memory.

tradeOffs.pro: KMP never backtracks and holds a strict O(N + M) ceiling even on pathological `AAAA...AB` inputs.
tradeOffs.con: KMP inspects every character sequentially, whereas Boyer-Moore skips large chunks and runs 3x–5x faster on typical English or log text.

tradeOffs.pro: Scans 10,000+ patterns simultaneously in one O(N + Z) pass.
tradeOffs.con: Dense transition tables (`states * alphabet_size`) consume significant RAM unless compressed with sparse maps or Double-Array Tries.

tradeOffs.factor: Rabin-Karp rolling hash collisions vs. simplicity
tradeOffs.pro: Extends naturally to 2D grids and variable-size rolling fingerprints (rsync/chunking).
tradeOffs.con: Hash collisions require an O(M) character-by-character verification, degrading worst-case to O(N * M) without double hashing.

failureModes.name: Adversarial O(N*M) backtracking DoS
failureModes.description: Naive matching or unverified rolling-hash collisions on crafted inputs like `"a" * 100000` against `"a" * 5000 + "b"` spike CPU to 100%.
failureModes.mitigation: Use KMP, Two-Way, or Aho-Corasick for untrusted inputs, or double-mod rolling hashes with strict step budgets.

failureModes.name: Aho-Corasick trie memory explosion
failureModes.description: Allocating a 256-entry `int[256]` array per Trie node for 500k UTF-8 pattern characters consumes gigabytes of heap.
failureModes.mitigation: Use byte-level transitions with sparse sorted arrays, hash maps, or a Double-Array Trie (DAT) representation.

failureModes.name: Missing overlapping matches via failure links
failureModes.description: Walking only `isEndOfWord` on the current Aho-Corasick node misses shorter suffixes (e.g., matching `"she"` misses `"he"`).
failureModes.mitigation: Precompute dictionary-suffix (output) links during BFS failure-link construction and traverse them on every match.

failureModes.name: Integer overflow in Rabin-Karp rolling hash
failureModes.description: Multiplying base powers without modular reduction at every step overflows 64-bit integers and breaks hash equality.
failureModes.mitigation: Apply `% MOD` (using a large prime like `1_000_000_007` or `2^61 - 1`) after every add/subtract/multiply step.

commonMistakes: Re-implementing KMP or Boyer-Moore in Python/Java loops for simple single-string checks when built-in C/SIMD `in` or `indexOf` is 10x faster.
Building Aho-Corasick failure links with DFS instead of BFS (failure links depend on shorter-depth ancestors already being resolved).
Confusing `LPS` (longest proper prefix-suffix) construction in KMP by failing to fall back `j = lps[j - 1]` inside a `while` loop.
Forgetting to verify exact character equality after a Rabin-Karp hash match.
Splitting streaming buffers naively at fixed 64 KB boundaries without carrying state or overlap, missing patterns that straddle chunk edges.

sections.content:
## The idea

Naive string matching throws away everything it learned when a mismatch occurs, backing up the text pointer and re-reading characters repeatedly. Modern string-matching algorithms eliminate redundant comparisons by precomputing structure in the **pattern(s)**: KMP and Aho-Corasick reuse matched prefixes via failure links, Boyer-Moore jumps past impossible alignments from right to left, and Rabin-Karp summarizes windows into O(1)-updatable rolling hashes.

## Concrete walkthrough

Tracing **KMP** on text `T = "ABABDABACDABABCABAB"` and pattern `P = "ABABCABAB"`:
1. **Build LPS table** for `P`: `[0, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` (e.g., at index 8 `'B'`, prefix `"ABAB"` matches suffix `"ABAB"`, length `4`).
2. **Scan `T` with pointer `i` (never decrements) and `P` with `j`**:
   - `i=0..3` matches `"ABAB"` (`j=4`).
   - At `i=4`, `T[4]='D' != P[4]='C'`. Instead of resetting `i` to `1`, KMP sets `j = lps[3] = 2`, keeping `i=4`.
   - `T[4]='D' != P[2]='A'`, so `j = lps[1] = 0`; still mismatch, so `i` advances to `5`.
3. **Match**: At `i=10..18`, `j` reaches `9 == len(P)`, reporting match at `i - j = 10`, then sets `j = lps[8] = 4` to continue searching for overlapping matches.

sections.content:
## Z-algorithm and Rabin-Karp mechanics

The **Z-algorithm** builds an array `Z[i]` storing the length of the longest substring starting at `i` that matches a prefix of `S`, using a `[L, R]` Z-box to reuse prior comparisons in O(N). Running it on `P + '$' + T` finds all occurrences where `Z[i] == len(P)` without explicit state transitions. **Rabin-Karp** instead maps a window of length `M` to `H = sum(c_k * B^(M-1-k)) mod Q` and slides in O(1) via `H_next = ((H - T[i]*B^(M-1)) * B + T[i+M]) mod Q`.

## Algorithm complexity and selection

| Algorithm | Preprocessing | Search (Avg / Worst) | Extra Space | Best Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Naive** | O(1) | O(N) / O(N*M) | O(1) | Tiny strings only |
| **KMP** | O(M) | O(N + M) / O(N + M) | O(M) | Streaming search, adversarial worst-case safety |
| **Boyer-Moore** | O(M + sigma) | O(N / M) / O(N*M) | O(M + sigma) | Fast single-pattern scan on large text/logs |
| **Rabin-Karp** | O(M) | O(N + M) / O(N*M) | O(1) or O(K) | Plagiarism, 2D pattern match, equal-length multi-match |
| **Aho-Corasick** | O(Sum M_i) | O(N + Z) / O(N + Z) | O(Sum M_i * sigma) | Multi-pattern DLP, WAF, keyword tagging |

## Failure modes

Two pitfalls dominate production deployments: **DFS failure-link bugs** in custom Aho-Corasick implementations (which leave deep failure pointers dangling) and **UTF-8 multi-byte boundary splits** when running byte-level automata over character-indexed rules—always normalize encoding (UTF-8 bytes vs. Unicode code points) before compiling patterns.

## Built-in runtimes vs. custom code

In **Java**, `String.indexOf` uses HotSpot SIMD intrinsics (`UseVectorizedMismatchIntrinsic`), outperforming hand-rolled pure-Java KMP on non-adversarial text; reach for `org.ahocorasick` or a custom KMP only for multi-pattern sets or streaming byte buffers. In **Python**, `str.find` / `in` executes C-level `fastsearch`; use `pyahocorasick` (C extension) when matching hundreds or thousands of patterns.

## Practical checklist

- Use native `String.indexOf` (Java) or `in` / `str.find` (Python) for single-pattern in-memory checks.
- Use Aho-Corasick whenever matching > 10–20 literal patterns simultaneously.
- Build Aho-Corasick failure links strictly via BFS and follow dictionary-suffix links for overlapping hits.
- Use KMP for O(M)-memory streaming across network/file chunk boundaries.
- Use double-hashing (`mod 1e9+7` and `mod 1e9+9`) in Rabin-Karp when collisions could cause O(N*M) slowdowns.

interviewProblems.title: String Matching Algorithms
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on String Matching Algorithms. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: String matching algorithms locate exact or multi-pattern substrings in linear or sublinear time without naive O(N*M) backtracking, using prefix tables (KMP), bad-character jumps (Boyer-Moore), rolling hashes (Rabin-Karp), or failure-link tries (Aho-Corasick).

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Text Stream (N) applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Output Collector.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Output Collector experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use KMP, Two-Way, or Aho-Corasick for untrusted inputs, or double-mod rolling hashes with strict step budgets.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Match the algorithm to the cardinality and alphabet: KMP guarantees O(N + M) worst-case for single patterns, Boyer-Moore/Two-Way powers fast single-pattern scans like grep/std::search, Rabin-Karp handles 2D/plagiarism hashing, and Aho-Corasick matches 10,000+ keywords simultaneously in a single O(N + Z) pass.
Avoid trap: Re-implementing KMP or Boyer-Moore in Python/Java loops for simple single-string checks when built-in C/SIMD `in` or `indexOf` is 10x faster.
Avoid trap: Building Aho-Corasick failure links with DFS instead of BFS (failure links depend on shorter-depth ancestors already being resolved).
When to reach for it: Single-pattern exact search with strict O(N + M) worst-case guarantees on adversarial or repetitive inputs (KMP / Z-algorithm).
When to reach for it: High-throughput single-pattern search in large ASCII/UTF-8 logs or source files where skipping ahead by M characters cuts cache reads (Boyer-Moore / Boyer-Moore-Horspool).

putItTogether.outcome: Compiling the 12,000 signatures into a single Aho-Corasick automaton cuts scan time to 1.4 ms per 1 MB payload in a single linear pass with zero backtracking.
